genesis.37.p1.b1.text: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.

genesis.37.p1.b2.text: When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, …

genesis.37.p1.b3.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, … so he made him a robe of many colors.

genesis.37.p1.b4.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.

genesis.37.p2.b1.text: Listen to this dream I had:

genesis.37.p2.b2.text: We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”

genesis.37.p2.b3.text: “Do you intend to reign over us?” … “Will you actually rule us?”

genesis.37.p2.b4.text: So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.

genesis.37.p3.b1.text: “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

genesis.37.p3.b2.text: “What is this dream that you have had? Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”

genesis.37.p3.b3.text: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept in mind what he had said.

genesis.37.p4.b1.text: Go now and see how your brothers and the flocks are faring, and bring word back to me.

genesis.37.p4.b2.text: And when Joseph arrived in Shechem,

genesis.37.p4.b4.text: “I am looking for my brothers,” … “Can you please tell me where they are pasturing their flocks?”

genesis.37.p4.b5.text: “They have moved on from here,” … “I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’”

genesis.37.p5.b1.text: Now Joseph’s brothers saw him in the distance, and before he arrived, they plotted to kill him.

genesis.37.p5.b2.text: “Here comes that dreamer!” … Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!

genesis.37.p5.b3.text: Do not shed his blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.

genesis.37.p5.b4.text: Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.

genesis.37.p6.b1.text: So when Joseph came to his brothers,

genesis.37.p6.b2.text: they stripped him of his robe—the robe of many colors he was wearing—

genesis.37.p6.b3.text: and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.

genesis.37.p7.b1.text: And as they sat down to eat a meal, they looked up … Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.

genesis.37.p7.b2.text: What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?

genesis.37.p7.b3.text: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.

genesis.37.p8.b1.text: So when the Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit

genesis.37.p8.b2.text: and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites,

genesis.37.p9.b1.text: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes,

genesis.37.p9.b2.text: The boy is gone! What am I going to do?

genesis.37.p9.b3.text: … slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.

genesis.37.p9.b4.text: We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.

genesis.37.p10.b1.text: It is my son’s robe! … Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!

genesis.37.p10.b2.text: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son many days.

genesis.37.p10.b3.text: I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.

genesis.37.p10.b4.text: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.
